contract.note: The contract tests only the two factual examples and treats 'clearest' as the speaker's judgement. Reading 'opening sentence' as the opening of the introduction is ordinary. Requiring a version available by March 14 is strict but fair.

evidence.note: Frontiers retraction notice dated Feb 16, 2024, citing concerns over AI-generated figures. This is a publisher disclosure. It confirms the rat paper was retracted before the post.
The original paper discloses that its images were made with Midjourney, and Figure 1 shows rat testes. This confirms the AI imagery.
A blog post dated Mar 17, 2024 identifies the lithium paper and its chatbot-style opening. It is three days after the period, so it does not establish the version available by Mar 14.

reviews.rationale: The rat example is supported: the paper had AI-generated images and was retracted on Feb 16, 2024. For the lithium example, the only readable account is dated Mar 17, after the target period, and no primary or pre-Mar 14 source was retrieved. The support condition needs both examples verified, and nothing contradicts either, so the overall outcome is unresolved.

semantics.note: This is a firm present-tense observation. The hedged follow-on ('may get a lot worse') is correctly left out.

contract.note: The plain reading, that generative AI put defective material into published science in early 2024, is ordinary. It neither demands proof of net harm across science nor stretches the claim in the speaker's favour. The period comes fairly from 'so far this year'.

evidence.note: The published paper (Feb 13, 2024) discloses that its images were generated by Midjourney. This establishes AI provenance in published work.
Bik's direct examination, dated Feb 15, 2024, documents anatomically and scientifically incorrect AI figures in the peer-reviewed paper.

reviews.rationale: Under the plain-reading contract, the evidence shows Midjourney-generated figures in a peer-reviewed paper published within the period. An independent examination found the figures scientifically incorrect. That meets the support condition, and the packet contains no counterevidence.
